brief: The Fed unanimously raised the fed funds target range 25bps to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike since July 2023 and the first under Chair Kevin Warsh. The FOMC statement says today's action supports a timelier return to the 2% goal, signaling the Committee sees inflation progress as too slow. Warsh said price stability is the Fed's predominant focus, since inflation has run above target for more than five years. The SEP's median dot plot adds one more quarter-point hike this year, puts year-end funds rate near 4.1%, holds through 2027, and removes the 2027 cut signaled in June, a shift tied more to economic resilience and geopolitically pressured commodity prices than to GDP and inflation forecasts, which moved only slightly. Warsh avoided specifying conditions for further hikes, with a tone closer to the Fed's usual pattern than his cryptic July remarks. CPI swaps-implied inflation fell 4 to 5bps after the announcement but stayed near year-to-date averages. Western Asset expects inflation to decline, though not enough to hit the Fed's target within a year. It expects further hikes but fewer than priced into the yield curve, and calls even two more hikes into 2027 a neutral environment for US fixed income.

cards.claim: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised the fed funds target rate range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, its first rate hike since July 2023.
cards.anchor: unanimously raised the fed funds target rate range by 25 basis points (bps) to 3.75%–4.00%, its first increase since July 2023

cards.claim: September's rate hike was the first FOMC policy move since Kevin Warsh became Fed Chair.
cards.anchor: the first under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh

cards.claim: The FOMC statement added language that today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2% inflation goal, signaling members see prior inflation progress as too slow.
cards.anchor: “today’s policy action will support a timelier return” to the Committee’s 2% goal indicates the members believe that progress on inflation has been too slow

cards.claim: Fed Chair Warsh said inflation has run above target for more than five years and that price stability is the Fed's predominant mandate focus.
cards.anchor: For more than five years, inflation has been running above target. So our predominant focus is on the price stability side of our mandate

cards.claim: The FOMC statement and Warsh's press conference comments described a strong economy with resilient domestic spending and a stable labor force, while noting inflation remains elevated.
cards.anchor: emphasized a strong economy with resilient domestic spending and a stable labor force, but noted that inflation remains elevated

cards.claim: The Fed's Summary of Economic Projections median dot plot shows one additional quarter-point rate hike expected this year.
cards.anchor: included expectations for one additional quarter-point rate hike this year, according to the median dot plot

cards.claim: The median dot plot's path projects the year-end fed funds rate around 4.1%.
cards.anchor: The plot's median path projects the year-end funds rate around 4.1%

cards.claim: The median dot plot holds the funds rate steady through 2027 and shows a single rate cut in 2028.
cards.anchor: holds steady through 2027 and shows a single cut in 2028

cards.claim: The September SEP removed the 2027 rate cut that had been signaled in the June projections.
cards.anchor: notably removing the 2027 cut that had been signaled in June

cards.claim: The expected policy rate over the next two years is now about 50 basis points higher than in the June SEP, even though GDP and inflation forecasts edged only slightly higher.
cards.anchor: the expected policy rate over the next two years is now some 50 bps higher

cards.claim: Expected inflation priced into CPI swaps fell 4 to 5 basis points following the September policy announcement, though it remains close to year-to-date averages.
cards.anchor: Expected inflation in Consumer Price Index (CPI) swaps fell 4 to 5 bps following the policy announcement, though it remains close to year-to-date averages.

cards.claim: Fed Chair Warsh avoided specifying the conditions under which the FOMC will or will not deliver additional rate hikes.
cards.anchor: Warsh avoided delineating the conditions under which the FOMC will or will not deliver on any additional rate hikes.

cards.claim: Warsh's September press conference comments were consistent with the FOMC's usual reaction function, unlike the more cryptic statements he made in July.
cards.anchor: his comments this time were consistent with the usual FOMC reaction function of the past rather than the more cryptic statements he made in July

cards.claim: Western Asset expects inflation to decline going forward, even if not at a pace that hits the Fed's target within the next year.
cards.anchor: Western Asset anticipates that inflation will decline going forward, even if not at a pace to hit the Fed’s target over the next year.

cards.claim: Western Asset believes it is unlikely that Fed rates will need to rise as high as currently priced into the yield curve, even though it expects further Fed rate increases.
cards.anchor: we believe it is unlikely that rates need to go as high as currently priced into the yield curve

cards.claim: Western Asset says that even if the Fed delivers two more rate hikes into 2027, it would still be a neutral environment for US fixed income given current pricing.
cards.anchor: our view is that it still would be a neutral environment for US fixed-income, given current pricing.
